sections.name: General Knowledge / Current Affairs of India and Goa

p1.title: Passage 1
paras: Fish in the open sea belong to no one until they are caught, and this simple fact lies at the heart of many fisheries' troubles. A fisherman who leaves young fish in the water so that they may grow and breed cannot be sure that he will be the one to benefit; a rival boat may simply catch them the next day. Each crew therefore has reason to take as much as it can, even when all of them can see that the stock is shrinking. Economists call such situations a tragedy of the commons, and the open ocean is perhaps its most familiar example.

The tragedy is not inevitable. Coastal communities in many parts of the world have long maintained customary rules: seasons when fishing stops, areas closed to nets, limits on the mesh size that lets small fish escape. The annual pause during the monsoon on India's western coast, when many fish breed, rests on a similar idea, though it is now enforced by law rather than by custom alone. Such rules work best when those who must obey them have had a hand in making them and can see that others are obeying too. Where enforcement is weak, or large trawlers from outside ignore the restrictions that local boats observe, trust collapses and the old race to the last fish resumes.

p2.title: Passage 2
paras: A map that showed every pebble and blade of grass would be as large as the country it described, and therefore useless. Its value lies precisely in what it leaves out. Scientific models share this character. An economist's model of a market, a climatologist's model of the atmosphere, or a physicist's picture of a gas as countless tiny colliding balls all simplify the world deliberately, ignoring features judged irrelevant to the question at hand. The model of a gas as bouncing balls is false in many respects, yet it predicts how pressure changes with temperature remarkably well.

The danger arises when the simplification is forgotten. A model built to answer one question may be pressed into service for another for which its omissions are crucial, and its users, impressed by its past successes, may mistake the map for the territory. Many failures of forecasting, in economics especially, have been traced not to bad mathematics but to assumptions that were reasonable in ordinary times and disastrous in unusual ones. The remedy is not to abandon models, without which no complex system could be studied at all, but to use them with an awareness of their boundaries. A good scientist asks not only what a model predicts, but what it was designed to ignore.

questions.q: Which title best suits the passage?
opts: The Life Cycle of Ocean Fish
The Commons at Sea and the Rules That Protect It
questions.why: Main idea: the open sea is a commons, but shared rules can prevent its tragedy.

questions.q: According to the passage, the monsoon pause on India's western coast is based on the fact that:
opts: Fish move to deeper water in the monsoon.
Fish prices fall sharply during the rains.
Many fish breed during that season.
Boats cannot be repaired during the rains.
questions.why: Detail: 'The annual pause during the monsoon on India's western coast, when many fish breed'.

questions.q: Which situation would the author most likely see as another example of a 'tragedy of the commons'?
opts: Villagers each grazing extra cattle on a shared pasture until the grass is exhausted.
A farmer overworking his own private field.
A cooperative fixing milk prices by a fat test.
A government selling a forest to a company.
questions.why: Inference: the tragedy arises when no one owns a shared resource, so each user takes as much as he can despite visible decline.

questions.q: The author mentions customary rules mainly to show that:
opts: Fishing should be banned throughout the year.
Coastal communities are hostile to outsiders.
The tragedy of the commons can be avoided through shared restraint.
Custom is always stronger than law.
questions.why: Purpose: they follow 'The tragedy is not inevitable'.

questions.q: The word "inevitable" most nearly means:
questions.why: Vocabulary: the tragedy is not certain to happen, as customary rules show.

questions.q: Which title best suits the passage?
opts: How to Draw an Accurate Map
questions.why: Main idea: models, like maps, are useful because they simplify, but their limits must be remembered.

questions.q: The model of a gas as bouncing balls is mentioned as an example of a model that:
opts: Is false in many respects yet predicts well.
questions.why: Detail: it 'is false in many respects, yet it predicts how pressure changes with temperature remarkably well'.

questions.q: To "mistake the map for the territory" means to:
opts: Draw a map larger than the country it shows.
Treat a simplified representation as if it were reality itself.
questions.why: Inference: users 'impressed by its past successes' forget 'the simplification'.

questions.q: According to the passage, many failures of economic forecasting have been traced to:
opts: Assumptions that suited ordinary times but failed in unusual ones.
questions.why: Detail: 'not to bad mathematics but to assumptions that were reasonable in ordinary times and disastrous in unusual ones'.

questions.q: The author's attitude towards scientific models is best described as:
opts: Indifferent to how they are used.
Appreciative of their usefulness but alert to their limits.
Contemptuous, since all models are false.
questions.why: Tone: 'The remedy is not to abandon models... but to use them with an awareness of their boundaries'.

questions.q: Choose the correct word: “The new health policy will ____ rural clinics positively.”
questions.why: 'Affect' is a verb meaning to influence; 'effect' is mostly a noun. GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: Identify the grammatically incorrect conditional sentence:
opts: If she would have studied, she would have passed.
If I had known, I would have told you.
If he comes, I will go with him.
If I were rich, I would travel.
questions.why: 'Would have' is not used in the if-clause: 'If she had studied'. GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: Which of the following is a simple sentence?
opts: Being ill, he stayed at home.
Though he was ill, he came.
He stayed at home because he was ill.
questions.why: It has one finite verb and one clause; the others are complex or compound. GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: Identify the error: “I look forward to meet you at the conference next week.”
questions.why: 'Look forward to' takes a gerund: 'to meeting'. GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: Choose the word closest in meaning to “inexorable”:
questions.why: 'Inexorable' means impossible to stop or persuade; relentless. GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: In September 2026, Smriti Mandhana became the leading run-scorer in women's T20 Internationals, overtaking:
questions.why: She reached the mark during the Asian Games cricket event. Sep 2026.

questions.q: On which date is Global Handwashing Day observed?
questions.why: First observed in 2008; WHO and UNICEF marked it in 2026 with a global webinar. Oct 2026.

questions.q: Rabindranath Tagore won the Nobel Prize in Literature in:
questions.why: He was the first Asian Nobel laureate, for 'Gitanjali'.

questions.q: The RBI approved Anup Kumar Saha in October 2026 as the next MD and CEO of which bank, from 1 January 2027?
questions.why: He succeeds Ashok Vaswani, whose term ends on 31 December 2026. Oct 2026.

questions.q: Which state launched India's first state-level Sports Genomics Programme to identify and train athletes using DNA data?
questions.why: It is led by the Gujarat Biotechnology Research Centre, ahead of the 2030 Commonwealth Games in Ahmedabad. Aug 2026.

questions.q: In the Henley Passport Index of October 2026, India's passport ranked:
questions.why: Up one place, though visa-free access fell to 55 destinations; Singapore is first. Oct 2026.

questions.q: INS Mangrol, commissioned in Mumbai in October 2026, is the third anti-submarine warfare shallow water craft of which class?
questions.why: It was built by Cochin Shipyard and named after Mangrol port in Gujarat. Oct 2026.

questions.q: Which became Madhya Pradesh's third cheetah habitat in October 2026, after Kuno and Gandhi Sagar?
questions.why: CM Mohan Yadav released two cheetahs into the reserve. Oct 2026.

questions.q: Who was appointed Governor of Uttarakhand in October 2026?
questions.why: The President appointed four new governors and moved two in the same order. Oct 2026.

questions.q: Who won the Sahitya Akademi Award 2025 for Konkani, announced in March 2026?
questions.why: He won for the essay collection 'Konkani Kavyem: Rupani Ani Rupakam'. Mar 2026.

questions.q: Statements: Some roses are flowers. No flowers are plants. Conclusions: I. Some roses are plants. II. Some roses are not plants.
questions.why: Checked against every possible diagram of the statements: I need not be true, II must be true. GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: What comes next? FGH, IJK, LMN, OPQ, …
questions.why: Each group starts 3 letters after the last one, with the same pattern inside: RST. GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: If SCHOOL is written as NQQJEU in a certain code, how is TEMPLE written in that code?
questions.why: In the code each letter moves 2 places forward and the word is then reversed: TEMPLE → GNROGV. GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: The present ages of Kavita and Meera are in the ratio 6 : 3. After 10 years the ratio will be 28 : 19. What is Meera's present age?
questions.why: Let the ages be 6k and 3k: (6k + 10)/(3k + 10) = 28/19 gives k = 3, so Meera is 9. GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: A shopkeeper marks an item 30% above cost and gives a 10% discount. What is the overall gain?
questions.why: Net = (1 + 30/100)(1 − 10/100) − 1 = 17%. GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: If 22 December 2024 was a Sunday, what day of the week was 4 March 2025?
questions.why: 72 days later; 72 mod 7 = 2, so count 2 days on from Sunday. GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: If 10 April 2025 was a Thursday, what day of the week was 20 June 2025?
questions.why: 71 days later; 71 mod 7 = 1, so count 1 day on from Thursday. GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: Statements: All roses are flowers. No flowers are plants. Conclusions: I. All roses are plants. II. Some plants are roses.
questions.why: Checked against every possible diagram of the statements: I need not be true, II need not be true. GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: Sita is the brother of Rekha. Kiran is the father of Sita. Kavita is the brother of Deepak. Deepak is the daughter of Rekha. Who is the uncle of Kavita?
questions.why: Draw the family tree from the statements; the answer is Sita. GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: Statements: All pens are books. All books are bags. Conclusions: I. Some pens are not bags. II. Some pens are bags.
questions.why: Checked against every possible diagram of the statements: I need not be true, II must be true. GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: Hahnemann's chief remedy for syphilis was:
questions.why: In 'The Chronic Diseases' Hahnemann treated syphilis with Mercurius; Thuja and Nitric acid were his remedies for sycosis and Sulphur for psora.

questions.q: According to §§74 and 75, the most deplorable and incurable of all chronic diseases are those produced by:
questions.why: §75: artificial chronic diseases caused by allopathic treatment are the most deplorable and incurable of all.

questions.q: According to Kent, if the first prescription has produced no action at all, the next prescription is:
opts: always a repetition of the same remedy in a higher potency
not a second prescription, but really a first prescription again
questions.why: Kent: the second prescription is the one that follows a prescription that has acted; if the first did nothing, the next is still a first prescription.

questions.q: Glonoinum is the homoeopathic preparation of:
questions.why: Glonoinum is nitroglycerine, proved by Hering; silver nitrate is Argentum nitricum.

questions.q: Religious mania with a desire to cut and tear things, and cold sweat on the forehead, points to:
questions.why: Veratrum album: religious mania, destructive impulses to cut and tear, with cold sweat on the forehead (Boericke).

questions.q: Which remedy is the chronic complement of Bryonia?
questions.why: Boericke gives Alumina (and Rhus tox) as complementary to Bryonia; Alumina is called its chronic.

questions.q: The letter 'D' before a potency number, as used in Germany and Europe, indicates the:
questions.why: D (decimal) is the European equivalent of X; 6D is the same as 6X.

questions.q: The abbreviation 'p.c.' on a prescription means:
questions.why: P.c. is post cibum, after food.

questions.q: The patient's statement 'I am always chilly' is classed as a:
questions.why: It describes the whole person's reaction to temperature, so it is a physical general.

questions.q: In Kent's Repertory, yawning is found in the chapter:
questions.why: Kent places yawning under Sleep, alongside sleepiness and sleeplessness.

questions.q: Total body water in an average adult man is about what share of body weight?
questions.why: About 60% of body weight is water: two-thirds intracellular (40%) and one-third extracellular (20%).

questions.q: Pancreatic trypsinogen is activated in the duodenum by:
questions.why: Enterokinase from the duodenal mucosa converts trypsinogen to trypsin, which then activates the other pancreatic proenzymes.

questions.q: The medium routinely used to culture Mycobacterium tuberculosis is:
opts: Thiosulphate citrate bile salt sucrose agar
questions.why: Egg-based Lowenstein-Jensen medium is the standard solid medium for M. tuberculosis; colonies appear in 2 to 8 weeks.

questions.q: On a chest X-ray, a homogeneous lobar opacity containing air bronchograms most suggests:
opts: Collapse due to an obstructing tumour
questions.why: Air bronchograms show air-filled bronchi within alveoli filled with exudate, the sign of consolidation; effusion and obstructive collapse do not show them.

questions.q: A person who has been vaccinated against hepatitis B but never infected will show in serum:
questions.why: The vaccine contains only HBsAg, so it induces anti-HBs alone; anti-HBc appears only after natural infection.

questions.q: Pitting of the nails with onycholysis is most characteristic of:
questions.why: Nail pitting, onycholysis and 'oil-drop' discolouration occur in psoriasis; iron deficiency gives koilonychia.

questions.q: A hypothyroid woman with a firm, painless goitre and strongly positive anti-thyroid peroxidase antibodies most likely has:
questions.why: Hashimoto's autoimmune thyroiditis, with anti-TPO antibodies, is the commonest cause of hypothyroidism in iodine-sufficient areas.

questions.q: Under IMNCI, fast breathing in a child aged 2 to 12 months is a respiratory rate of:
questions.why: Cut-offs are 60/min under 2 months, 50/min for 2–12 months and 40/min for 1–5 years.

questions.q: Bed-wetting in an irritable child who picks at the nose, grinds the teeth in sleep and has a canine hunger calls for:
questions.why: Cina is the classic worm remedy with nose-boring, teeth grinding, ravenous hunger and nocturnal enuresis.

questions.q: Under the current UIP, fractional IPV (fIPV, 0.1 mL intradermal) is given at:
questions.why: Since 2023 a third fIPV dose at 9 months has been added to the 6- and 14-week doses.

questions.q: Conjunctivitis with profuse, acrid, burning tears but a bland nasal discharge calls for:
questions.why: Euphrasia has acrid lachrymation with bland coryza, the reverse of Allium cepa.

questions.q: A painless ulcer over the heel or the head of the first metatarsal in a patient with diabetic or leprotic neuropathy is a:
questions.why: Loss of sensation over pressure points leads to painless perforating trophic ulcers.

questions.q: Convulsions with opisthotonus and risus sardonicus, with the mind clear between the fits, suggest poisoning by:
questions.why: Strychnine blocks glycine inhibition in the spinal cord, causing tetanic convulsions while consciousness is preserved between fits.

questions.q: According to Nysten's rule, rigor mortis passes off:
opts: in the reverse order of its appearance
all over the body at the same time
in the same order in which it appeared
questions.why: Rigor appears in eyelids, face, neck, trunk, upper then lower limbs, and passes off in the same sequence.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT one of the autonomous boards constituted under the National Commission for Homoeopathy Act, 2020?
opts: Medical Assessment and Rating Board for Homoeopathy
Board of Ethics and Registration for Homoeopathy
questions.why: The NCH Act sets up three autonomous boards: Education, Medical Assessment and Rating, and Ethics and Registration; pharmacopoeia work lies outside it.
